title: Counted, but not landed
subtitle: Share of U.S. farm operations vs. share of U.S. farmland, by producer race and ethnicity, 2022 Census of Agriculture. Farms with at least one Black producer are 1.51% of operations and hold 0.49% of the land.

order: Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander

connector.direction_note: Segment points LEFT when a group's land share falls short of its share of farms, RIGHT when it exceeds it. Direction, not just length, carries the claim.

annotations.text: 0.49% of farmland on 1.51% of farms — a land share 3.1x smaller than the farm-count share. Average 150 acres vs. 463 for the U.S. as a whole.
The one reversal: 6.34% of farmland on 2.14% of farms. 37% of those acres are in Arizona alone — largely arid reservation rangeland, not an indicator of comparable land security.
96.3% of operations, 93.6% of acres. The reference point, not a residual.

Trend, same series 2002→2022: the Black land share rose 0.409% → 0.491% while Black-operated farms fell 30,605 → 28,723. The land-share-to-farm-share ratio sat at 0.27–0.28 for fifteen years and reached 0.33 only in 2022 — partly consolidation, not only access.
Groups OVERLAP and must never be stacked: a farm with a Black and a White producer is counted in both rows.

Definitional break at 2017: the Census switched from 'operators' (≤3/farm) to 'producers' (≤4/farm). Producer head-counts jump across the break; operations and acres — the two series charted here — do not.

source_note: USDA NASS Census of Agriculture, 2022 (QuickStats bulk mirror, qs.census2022.txt.gz), national level, DOMAIN_DESC = TOTAL. Series: 'PRODUCERS, <group> - NUMBER OF OPERATIONS' and '- ACRES OPERATED'; denominators 'FARM OPERATIONS - ...' (1,900,487 farms; 880,100,848 acres). Computed by analysis/penniman/compute.py.
